framings.label: Midterms as voter verdict
framings.description: Frames data center opposition as a decisive electoral force, citing ousted incumbents, flipped states and ballot results as a message from voters.

framings.label: Industry response and damage control
framings.description: Covers how tech companies and suppliers react to the backlash through pledges, rebranding, retrofitting ideas, warnings about slower expansion, and arguments that the anger is political rather than anti-tech.

framings.label: Backlash as business and market risk
framings.description: Treats the backlash as a financial and strategic matter, examining effects on energy stocks, IPOs, the trillion-dollar buildout, and which large or small firms gain or lose.

framings.label: European street protest and direct action
framings.description: Reports on physical demonstrations and site break-ins across Europe, presenting the opposition as a spreading, coordinated protest movement.

framings.label: Regulation, politicians and civil liberties
framings.description: Focuses on political targets and policy consequences, including protests at a senator's home, expected tougher rules, and arguments about civil rights and accountability of big tech deals.
